title: Chicken Soup
description: A classic Continental chicken soup made with a clear homemade stock, tender shredded chicken, and delicate vegetables. Light, refined, and perfect as a comforting starter or light main course.

ingredients.title: For the Chicken Stock (Base)
items: Whole chicken – 1 (about 1.2 kg), cut into pieces
Large onion – 1, halved (leave skin on for color)

ingredients.title: For the Soup
items: All-purpose flour – 1 tbsp (optional, for slight thickening)
Dry white wine – 100 ml (optional but adds refinement)
Salt and white pepper – to taste
Fresh parsley or chives – finely chopped (for garnish)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Chicken Stock
steps: Combine chicken, cold water, and all aromatics in a large stockpot.
Bring to a gentle simmer — never a rolling boil (this keeps the stock clear).
Skim foam frequently for the first 15 minutes.
Strain through a fine sieve or muslin cloth.
Skim any fat off the surface. Set aside or refrigerate overnight for clarity.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Make the Soup Base
steps: In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat butter and olive oil over medium-low heat.
Add diced onion, carrot, celery, and leek — sweat gently until translucent (no browning).
Stir in flour (if using) and cook for 1 minute to form a light roux.
Deglaze with white wine; reduce by half.
Add hot clarified stock and simmer 10–15 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in shredded chicken and cream (optional).
Season with salt and white pepper.

instruction.title: Step 3 – To Serve
steps: Garnish lightly with chopped parsley or chives.
Serve with toasted baguette slices or buttered brioche croutons.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot with toasted baguette slices.
Enjoy as a light main course or elegant starter.

chefTips: A crystal-clear stock is the hallmark of a professional Continental soup.
Clarity and depth of flavor define Continental soups — avoid over-seasoning.
Use fresh herbs only; dried herbs dull the refined flavor profile.
A dash of sherry or white wine before serving adds sophistication.
For a luxury variant, add a poached quail egg or a few drops of truffle oil just before serving.
